offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first through third); Class E Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
On any road, street, alley, waterway, or other premise open to the public
While under the influence of alcohol, a drug, marijuana, or any intoxicant
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours (first); 45 consecutive days (second); 120 consecutive days (third); 150 consecutive days (fourth+)
enhancements: BAC .20 or higher (minimum 7 consecutive days first offense)
Child under 18 in vehicle (mandatory minimum 30 days, $1,000 additional fine)
Fourth or subsequent offense (Class E Felony)
notes: Implied consent under Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-10-406. License revocation: 1 year (first), 2 years (second), 6 years (third), 8 years (fourth+). $100 alcohol and drug treatment fee assessed on each conviction.

elements: Defendant drove or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment; 7 consecutive days if BAC .20+
notes: One-year license revocation. Must attend alcohol/drug treatment program. Eligible for restricted license after certain conditions met.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second/third); Class E Felony (fourth+)
penalty_min: 45 consecutive days (second); 120 consecutive days (third); 150 consecutive days (fourth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 45 consecutive days (second); 120 consecutive days (third); 150 consecutive days (fourth+)
notes: Second offense: 2-year license revocation. Third: 6-year revocation. Fourth+: 8-year revocation. Vehicle forfeiture possible on third or subsequent offense.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_min: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of a drug or marijuana
Or any intoxicant, drug, or substance affecting the central nervous system
To a degree that impairs the defendant's ability to safely drive
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must show actual impairment. Includes prescription medications if they impair driving ability.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common DUI plea-down. Adds 4 points to driving record.

statute_title: Leaving Scene of Accident — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (injury); Class E Felony (serious injury); Class D Felony (death)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant knowingly failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving the scene of a property-damage-only accident is a Class C Misdemeanor under § 55-10-102.

offense_class: Class B Felony (intoxication); Class C Felony (reckless)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
As the proximate result of intoxication or reckless conduct
Caused the death of another person
enhancements: Intoxication (Class B Felony rather than Class C)
notes: Vehicular homicide by intoxication is a Class B Felony. Vehicular homicide by reckless conduct is a Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While intoxicated or in a reckless manner
Caused serious bodily injury to another person
notes: Tennessee does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths are charged as vehicular homicide (§ 39-13-213). Vehicular assault covers serious injuries.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended, Canceled, or Revoked
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Class A Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended, canceled, or revoked
Defendant had knowledge or should have known of the suspension
notes: DUI-related suspensions carry additional penalties. Habitual motor vehicle offender designation may apply after multiple convictions.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (on foot); Class E Felony (by vehicle); Class D Felony (risk of death)
penalty_max: 11 months 29 days (on foot); 6 years (vehicle); 12 years (risk of death)
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle or on foot
A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant intentionally fled or attempted to elude the officer
enhancements: Evasion by motor vehicle (Class E Felony)
Creating risk of death to bystanders (Class D Felony)
notes: Evading arrest by vehicle is a Class E Felony. If the flight creates a risk of death to innocent bystanders, it becomes a Class D Felony.

statute_title: Simple Possession or Casual Exchange of Controlled Substance
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
In an amount for personal use
Without a valid prescription
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense within 7 years (Class E Felony under § 39-17-418(e))
notes: Simple possession is a Class A Misdemeanor for first and second offenses. Third offense within 7 years becomes a Class E Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first/second); Class E Felony (third+ within 7 years)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed marijuana
In an amount for personal use (1/2 oz or less for casual exchange)
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense within 7 years (Class E Felony)
notes: Marijuana is not decriminalized in Tennessee. Possession of 1/2 oz or less is simple possession. Greater amounts may support intent to distribute.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first/second); Class E Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
In an amount for personal use
Without lawful authorization
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense within 7 years (Class E Felony)
notes: Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance. Larger amounts may support manufacturing, delivery, or sale charges.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first/second); Class E Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
In an amount for personal use
Without lawful authorization
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense within 7 years (Class E Felony)
notes: Meth is a major enforcement priority in Tennessee. Possession of meth manufacturing components may trigger additional charges.

statute_title: Manufacturing, Delivery, Sale, or Possession with Intent
offense_class: Varies by schedule and amount: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III); Class D Felony (Schedule IV); Class E Felony (Schedule V/VI/VII)
penalty_min: 8 years (Class B); 3 years (Class C); 2 years (Class D); 1 year (Class E)
penalty_max: 30 years (Class B); 15 years (Class C); 12 years (Class D); 6 years (Class E)
fine_max: $100,000 or more depending on substance and quantity
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, sold, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance
Classification depends on the schedule and amount of the substance
notes: Fines can reach $500,000 for large quantities. Drug-free school zone enhancements add penalties. Tennessee Drug Offender Registry may apply.

statute_title: Sale or Delivery of Controlled Substance
offense_class: Varies by schedule: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III)
elements: Defendant sold or delivered a controlled substance
To another person
notes: Sale or delivery carries the same range as manufacturing and possession with intent under § 39-17-417.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III)
elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
The substance was listed in the schedules of controlled substances
enhancements: Manufacturing in the presence of a child
notes: Tennessee Meth-Free Tennessee Act provides enhanced penalties for methamphetamine production. Manufacturing in the presence of a child triggers additional charges.

statute_title: Use or Possession of Drug Paraphernalia
elements: Defendant used or possessed with intent to use drug paraphernalia

To plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, process, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale, or introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia is a Class A Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a Class E Felony.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Manufacture, Deliver, or Sell
offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I/II); Class C Felony (Schedule III); Class D Felony (Schedule IV)
penalty_min: 8 years (Class B); 3 years (Class C); 2 years (Class D)
penalty_max: 30 years (Class B); 15 years (Class C); 12 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to manufacture, deliver, or sell
Intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, or other circumstances
notes: Intent to distribute is typically inferred from large quantities, packaging materials, scales, large amounts of cash, or communications.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With premeditation and deliberation
Or during the perpetration of certain enumerated felonies (felony murder)
Or by use of a bomb or destructive device
enhancements: Aggravating factors may support death penalty
Felony murder (killing during commission of rape, robbery, burglary, kidnapping, arson, etc.)
notes: Tennessee has the death penalty. First-degree murder includes premeditated murder and felony murder. Minimum sentence is life imprisonment with possibility of parole.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Knowingly
Without premeditation
notes: Second-degree murder is a knowing killing without premeditation. Distinguished from first-degree murder by absence of premeditation and deliberation.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another
In a state of passion produced by adequate provocation
Sufficient to lead a reasonable person to act in an irrational manner
notes: Heat of passion killing. Adequate provocation must be sufficient to excite a reasonable person to act irrationally.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
A substantial and unjustifiable risk was disregarded
notes: Tennessee uses 'criminally negligent homicide' rather than 'involuntary manslaughter.' Also see reckless homicide (§ 39-13-215) as Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class C Felony (serious bodily injury); Class D Felony (deadly weapon); Class D Felony (strangulation)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused serious bodily injury to another
Or used or displayed a deadly weapon
Or caused bodily injury by strangulation or attempted strangulation
notes: Aggravated assault involving serious bodily injury is a Class C Felony. Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon is a Class D Felony.

elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or intentionally or knowingly caused another to reasonably fear imminent bodily injury
Or intentionally or knowingly caused physical contact with another that a reasonable person would find extremely offensive or provocative
enhancements: Against certain protected classes (nurses, emergency personnel)
notes: Simple assault is a Class A Misdemeanor. Assault against certain professionals (nurses, first responders) may carry enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused bodily injury to another person
Or caused physical contact that a reasonable person would find offensive
notes: Tennessee combines assault and battery under the single assault statute. No separate battery offense.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly committed theft
From the person of another
By violence or putting the person in fear
notes: Robbery is theft from a person by violence or fear. Distinguished from aggravated robbery and especially aggravated robbery.

elements: Defendant committed robbery as defined in § 39-13-401
Accomplished with a deadly weapon or by display of any article used or fashioned to lead the victim to believe it to be a deadly weapon
Or the victim suffered serious bodily injury
notes: Especially aggravated robbery (§ 39-13-403) using a firearm or causing serious bodily injury is a Class A Felony with 15-60 year range.

elements: Defendant knowingly removed or confined another person
Without the victim's consent
To facilitate commission of a felony, interfere with government function, inflict bodily injury, or terrorize
notes: Aggravated kidnapping (§ 39-13-304) involving a deadly weapon, serious bodily injury, or ransom is a Class B Felony. Especially aggravated kidnapping (§ 39-13-305) is a Class A Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly damaged any structure
By means of a fire or explosion
Without the consent of all persons who have a possessory, proprietary or security interest in the property
enhancements: Occupied building (aggravated arson § 39-14-302, Class A Felony)
notes: Aggravated arson (§ 39-14-302) involving occupied structures, bodily injury, or firefighter injury is a Class A Felony with 15-60 year range.

elements: Defendant intended to commit first-degree murder
Defendant acted with the intent to complete the crime
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The victim survived
notes: Attempted first-degree murder is classified one class below the completed offense — Class A Felony. Attempted second-degree murder is a Class B Felony.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly committed an assault
Using or displaying a deadly weapon
enhancements: Serious bodily injury resulting (elevates to Class C Felony)
notes: A deadly weapon includes firearms, knives, and any instrument capable of causing death or serious bodily harm when used as a weapon.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor ($1,000 or less); Class E Felony ($1,000-$2,500); Class D Felony ($2,500-$10,000); Class C Felony ($10,000-$60,000); Class B Felony ($60,000-$250,000); Class A Felony ($250,000+)
penalty_max: 11 months 29 days to 60 years depending on value
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exercised control over property of another
Without the owner's effective consent
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: Tennessee's theft statute consolidates larceny, embezzlement, false pretenses, and other theft offenses. Value thresholds determine the offense class.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($2,500-$10,000); Class C Felony ($10,000-$60,000); Class B Felony ($60,000+)
penalty_max: 12 years (Class D); 15 years (Class C); 30 years (Class B)
elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property exceeded $2,500
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Felony theft begins at $1,000 in Tennessee. Values over $2,500 are Class D Felonies or higher.

elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property was $1,000 or less
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Prior theft convictions may enhance classification
notes: Theft of $1,000 or less is a Class A Misdemeanor in Tennessee.

elements: Defendant concealed unpurchased merchandise
From a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the property without paying
notes: Penalties follow the same value thresholds as general theft. Civil liability to the merchant also applies.

elements: Defendant entered a building other than a habitation
Without the effective consent of the property owner
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault
notes: Standard burglary applies to non-habitation buildings. Aggravated burglary (§ 39-14-403) of a habitation is a Class C Felony. Especially aggravated burglary (§ 39-14-404) is a Class B Felony.

elements: Defendant entered a habitation
Without the effective consent of the property owner
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault
notes: Aggravated burglary of a habitation is a Class C Felony. Especially aggravated burglary (victim present and defendant has a weapon) is a Class B Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exercised control over a motor vehicle
Without the owner's consent
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Value of vehicle may increase classification
notes: Motor vehicle theft is a minimum Class E Felony regardless of vehicle value.

offense_class: Same classification as theft based on value
elements: Defendant received, concealed, or disposed of property
Knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Penalties mirror theft classifications based on value of stolen property received.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor ($1,000 or less); Class E Felony ($1,000-$2,500); Class D Felony ($2,500-$10,000); Class C Felony ($10,000-$60,000); Class B Felony ($60,000+)
penalty_max: 11 months 29 days to 30 years depending on value
elements: Defendant knowingly caused damage to or destroyed real or personal property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Restitution is typically ordered. Vandalism of a place of worship carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class B Misdemeanor (habitation); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant entered or remained on property of another
Without the owner's consent
After receiving notice to leave or against clearly posted signage
enhancements: Trespass on a habitation (Class B Misdemeanor)
notes: Criminal trespass on property is a Class C Misdemeanor. On a habitation is a Class B Misdemeanor. Aggravated criminal trespass is a Class B Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant knowingly damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Tennessee uses the vandalism statute rather than a separate criminal mischief statute.

elements: Defendant committed an assault as defined in § 39-13-101
Against a domestic abuse victim as defined in § 36-3-601
notes: Domestic abuse victim includes current/former spouse, person living together, person related by blood or marriage, dating relationship, or person with a child in common.

elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused bodily injury to a domestic abuse victim
As defined in § 36-3-601
enhancements: Aggravated domestic assault with weapon or serious injury (§ 39-13-102)
notes: Tennessee combines assault and battery under one statute. Domestic context triggers the domestic assault classification.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (endangerment); Class D Felony (serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly, other than by accidental means, treated a child under 18 in a manner
That resulted in injury or created a risk of injury
notes: Mandatory reporting by professionals. Aggravated child abuse (§ 39-15-402) is a Class A Felony.

elements: Defendant committed child abuse as defined in § 39-15-401
Resulting in serious bodily injury
Or used a deadly weapon
Or the child was under 8 years old and serious bodily injury resulted
notes: Aggravated child abuse is among the most seriously punished offenses in Tennessee. Treated as a violent offense for sentencing purposes.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class E Felony (subsequent)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation (Class E Felony)
notes: Violation of an order of protection is a separate criminal offense even if the underlying conduct is not otherwise criminal.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class E Felony (second or involving minor victim)
elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly followed or harassed another person
In a manner that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or harassed
enhancements: Second or subsequent conviction (Class E Felony)
Victim is a minor (Class E Felony)
Aggravated stalking with credible threat (Class E Felony)
notes: Aggravated stalking (§ 39-17-315(c)) involving a credible threat of death or serious bodily injury is a Class E Felony.

elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in conduct directed toward another person
That seriously alarms, annoys, threatens, or terrorizes the victim
The conduct serves no legitimate purpose
notes: Includes threatening communications, anonymous calls, and repeated unwanted contact.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of Elderly or Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (abuse/neglect); Class E Felony (exploitation $1,000-$10,000); Class D Felony (exploitation $10,000+)
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited an elderly or vulnerable adult
The victim was age 60 or older or a vulnerable adult
The conduct caused harm or risk of harm
notes: Mandatory reporting of suspected abuse. Financial exploitation is prosecuted based on the amount taken.

statute_title: Unlawful Carrying or Possession of a Weapon
offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (first); Class B Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant carried a weapon on or about their person
With the intent to go armed
In violation of location or eligibility restrictions
notes: Tennessee allows permit-less carry for persons 21+ (18+ for military). This statute primarily applies to prohibited locations and prohibited persons.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class E Felony (non-violent felony); Class B Felony (violent felony)
elements: Defendant possessed or carried a handgun or firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony involving force, violence, or a dangerous weapon
Or convicted of certain drug offenses
enhancements: Prior violent felony conviction (Class B Felony)
notes: Persons convicted of violent felonies face Class B Felony charges. Non-violent felons face Class E Felony charges.

statute_title: Carrying a Weapon in Prohibited Location
elements: Defendant carried a weapon
In a location prohibited by law (schools, government buildings, etc.)
notes: Prohibited locations include schools, courthouses, government buildings, and establishments that serve alcohol for on-premises consumption.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class E Felony if in certain areas
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless manner
Creating a risk of harm to persons
enhancements: Discharge within a municipality or residential area
notes: Reckless discharge in a populated area is treated more seriously. May also be charged as reckless endangerment.

elements: Defendant knowingly transferred or used the personal identifying information of another
Without the other person's consent
With intent to commit or facilitate the commission of a crime
enhancements: Multiple victims (trafficking in identifying information, Class C Felony)
notes: Trafficking in personal identifying information involving five or more victims is a Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to their own use
Without authorization
notes: Embezzlement is prosecuted under the general theft statute in Tennessee.

elements: Defendant forged a writing
With intent to defraud or harm another
The writing, if genuine, would create or transfer legal rights or obligations
notes: Includes forging checks, deeds, wills, contracts, and other legal documents.

elements: Defendant made or altered a writing or object
So it appeared to have value or authenticity that it does not have
With intent to defraud
notes: Criminal simulation covers counterfeiting of documents and objects. Federal charges may also apply for currency counterfeiting.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class E Felony ($1,000+)
elements: Defendant issued a check or order
Knowing at the time there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Presumption of knowledge and intent if check not made good within 10 days of notice.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented a false or fraudulent insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
The statement or claim was material
notes: Includes healthcare fraud, auto insurance fraud, and workers' compensation fraud.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of Credit or Debit Card
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, revoked, or not their own
With intent to defraud
notes: Credit card fraud is a Class E Felony regardless of the amount obtained.

offense_class: Class B Felony (over $10,000); Class C Felony ($10,000 or less)
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction involving proceeds of a specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property involved was derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote the activity or conceal the source
notes: Also subject to federal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1956.

elements: Defendant obtained property by deception
Defendant created a false impression of fact, law, or value
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud is prosecuted as theft by deception. Specific fraud statutes may also apply (insurance, securities, etc.).

elements: Defendant had unlawful sexual contact with a victim
By force or coercion
Without the victim's consent
enhancements: Victim under 13 (aggravated sexual battery § 39-13-504, Class B Felony)
notes: Sexual battery is Tennessee's equivalent of sexual assault. Aggravated sexual battery (§ 39-13-504) is a Class B Felony.

elements: Defendant engaged in unlawful sexual penetration of a victim
By force or coercion
While armed with a weapon, or causing bodily injury, or the victim was under 13
notes: Rape (§ 39-13-503) is a Class B Felony. Aggravated rape (§ 39-13-502) is a Class A Felony. Lifetime supervision may be required.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally exposed their genitals or buttocks
In a public place or in a place viewable from a public place
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class A Misdemeanor)
In presence of a minor (enhanced penalties)
notes: May trigger sex offender registration depending on circumstances.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class E Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant solicited or paid for sexual activity
Or patronized a person engaged in prostitution
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class E Felony)
Solicitation of a minor (Class B Felony)
notes: Patronizing prostitution of a minor is a Class B Felony. Second offense for adult prostitution becomes a Class E Felony.

statute_title: Offense of Sexual Exploitation of a Minor
offense_class: Class B Felony (production); Class C Felony (distribution); Class D Felony (possession)
penalty_min: 8 years (Class B); 3 years (Class C); 2 years (Class D)
penalty_max: 30 years (Class B); 15 years (Class C); 12 years (Class D)
elements: Defendant produced, distributed, or possessed material depicting a minor in sexually explicit conduct
Defendant knew or should have known the material depicted a minor
notes: Especially aggravated sexual exploitation (§ 39-17-1005) involving 50+ images or distribution is a Class B Felony. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, update, or verify registration information
notes: Tennessee Sex Offender Registry requires lifetime registration for most sex offenses.

offense_class: Class E Felony (defendant 4+ years older); Class E Felony (mitigated statutory rape, 5-9 year gap); Class D Felony (aggravated, 10+ year gap)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with a victim
The victim was at least 13 but less than 18
The defendant was at least 4 years older than the victim
enhancements: Age gap of 10+ years (aggravated statutory rape, Class D Felony)
notes: Age of consent in Tennessee is 18. Mitigated statutory rape applies when age gap is 5-9 years. Aggravated applies for 10+ year gap.

elements: Defendant in a public place intentionally caused a public annoyance or alarm
By engaging in fighting, violent or threatening behavior
Or creating a hazardous or physically offensive condition
notes: Common low-level offense. Often combined with other charges.

elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or obstructed a law enforcement officer
From effecting a stop, frisk, halt, arrest, or search
By using force against the officer or another
notes: Applies to resistance by force. Passive resistance alone may not constitute this offense. Flight from arrest is charged separately as evading.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (concealing misdemeanant); Class C Felony (concealing Class A/B felon); Class E Felony (concealing other felon)
penalty_max: 11 months 29 days to 15 years depending on underlying offense
elements: Defendant, with intent to hinder the apprehension, prosecution, or punishment of another
Harbored, concealed, or provided a weapon, transportation, disguise, or other means of avoiding apprehension
enhancements: Severity depends on the classification of the underlying offense
notes: Obstruction of justice in Tennessee is charged under multiple statutes including tampering with evidence and hindering prosecution.

offense_class: Up to 10 days imprisonment and $50 fine (direct); varies for indirect
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or engaged in disorderly, contemptuous, or insolent behavior in court
Tending to interrupt proceedings or impair respect for the court
notes: Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place under the influence of alcohol or drugs
To the degree that the defendant was a danger to themselves or others
Or was unreasonably annoying people in the vicinity
notes: Officers may use their discretion to take the person to a detoxification center rather than arrest.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying); Class E Felony (felony underlying)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court at a specified time
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Class E Felony)
notes: Bond may be forfeited and bench warrant issued. Separate offense from the underlying charge.

offense_class: Class D Felony (false report of crime); Class A Misdemeanor (other false reports)
elements: Defendant initiated or circulated a report or warning of a crime
Knowing it to be false or baseless
And likely to cause public alarm or inconvenience
notes: Filing a false report of a crime is a Class D Felony. Other types of false reports may be misdemeanors.

statute_title: Threat of Mass Violence or Terroristic Threat
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (threat of mass violence on school property)
elements: Defendant communicated a threat to commit a crime of violence
With intent to place the victim or public in fear
The threat was credible
enhancements: Threat of mass violence on school property (Class D Felony)
notes: Threats of mass violence at schools are treated as Class D Felonies under Tennessee law.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath
In an official proceeding
The statement was material
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Aggravated perjury (§ 39-16-703) in a proceeding where another is charged with a criminal offense is a Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's vote, opinion, judgment, or action
notes: Both the person offering and the official accepting may be charged.

offense_class: Class E Felony (misdemeanor custody); Class D Felony (felony custody); Class C Felony (with force/weapon)
penalty_min: 1 year (Class E); 2 years (Class D); 3 years (Class C)
penalty_max: 6 years (Class E); 12 years (Class D); 15 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant was in lawful custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
enhancements: Use of force or weapon (Class C Felony)
notes: Sentence for escape runs consecutively to any sentence being served.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class E Felony (subsequent or aggravated)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly tortured, maimed, or killed an animal
Or failed to provide necessary food, water, or care
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class E Felony)
notes: Aggravated cruelty to animals is a Class E Felony. Includes animal fighting under § 39-14-203.

penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
The violation was established by a preponderance of the evidence
notes: Court may revoke probation and order incarceration. Graduated sanctions may be imposed for technical violations.

elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Board of Parole makes revocation decisions. Defendant may be returned to serve the remainder of the sentence.

statute_title: Criminal Responsibility for Conduct of Another
elements: A crime was committed by another person
Defendant, acting with intent to promote or assist the commission of the offense
Solicited, directed, aided, or attempted to aid another person to commit the offense
